subject: Problem in the interpretation of F1*F2

messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: Problem in the interpretation of F1*F2
parts:
Hello Phil,


model.combo <- mirt.model('
F1 = 1-16
F2 = 17-32
(F1*F2) = 1-8')

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mirt/mirt.pdf   (page no. 58)

In the above code, how to interpret  (F1*F2)=1-8 ?



Regards,

Irshad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Problem in the interpretation of F1*F2
parts:
Hi Irshad,

The bracket terms represent (centred) product terms between the factors, and are used to model non-monotonic relationships. If you were using the 2PL model parametrization, then item 1 in your syntax would yield

logit(P) = a * θ1 * θ2 + d

Since the thetas are centred the interpretation is fairly straightforward and describes how pairs of thetas cause systematic curvature in the plots (when a is positive, individuals with high θ1 and θ2 will have high probability of answering correctly, but so will individuals with low θ1 and θ2....so for ability tests, this may not be desirable). Cheers.

Phil
